question: How many new-mover leads are in Lancaster County?
html:
Lancaster County new-mover leads

The context has no Lancaster County figure. The ad plan counts new movers only for the nine-county Pennsylvania core as a whole, so a Lancaster number would be a guess (Punctual Pros ad plan).

What the data does show

  • About 2,300 arm's-length residential sales a month across the nine-county Pennsylvania core, from county deed records. Each is a household that must choose an HVAC, plumbing and electrical provider within months (Punctual Pros ad plan, Oct 6, 2026).
  • About 1,150 sales a month on the Jersey Shore (Punctual Pros ad plan).
  • About one in three Pennsylvania core buyers bought a pre-1980 home (Punctual Pros ad plan).
  • The plan assumes a 1.0% lead rate per mail piece. It sets this below the 4-5% prospect response rate the ANA reports. This is an assumption, not a measured rate (Punctual Pros ad plan).
  • Lancaster is one of the nine core counties and holds a confirmed tri-brand site on Running Pump Rd (Punctual Pros market profile, Sep 24, 2026).

Prospects versus leads

"New movers" and "leads" are different things:

MeasurePA core (all nine counties)Lancaster County
New-mover households per month~2,300Not in context
Mail leads per month at 1.0%~23 (est.)Not in context

The ~23 is simple arithmetic on the plan's assumed rate. Treat it as an estimate until the mail test reads out.

Why not prorate

  • One shortcut would be to split the 2,300 by Lancaster's share of households. The market profile gives about 965k occupied homes for the core, but the excerpt does not show Lancaster's share.
  • Sales volume also may not track households, so a prorated figure could mislead.
  • The Census building permits snapshot does not list Lancaster among the counties shown. Permits measure new construction, not resales, so they would not answer this question anyway.

Data that would answer it

  • Lancaster County deed records filtered to arm's-length residential sales, by month. This is the same source the plan used for the core total.
  • ServiceTitan tracking-number and QR responses from mail drop 1, read by Lancaster zip. This gives actual leads rather than modelled ones.
  • The Lancaster share of the pre-1980 buyer segment, which the plan uses to target the Ben Franklin offer.

Next actions

  • Pull the Lancaster County deed extract for the last 12 months. Report monthly arm's-length residential sales and the pre-1980 share.
  • Cut mail drop 1 response by county in ServiceTitan. Report Lancaster leads and booked jobs against the 10% new-mover holdout.
  • Replace the 1.0% lead-rate assumption with the measured Lancaster response once the week-4 read is in.
  • Add a county column to the new-mover list so later questions like this one can be answered directly.
markdown:
# Lancaster County new-mover leads

The context has no Lancaster County figure. The ad plan counts new movers only for the nine-county Pennsylvania core as a whole, so a Lancaster number would be a guess (Punctual Pros ad plan).

## What the data does show

- About 2,300 arm's-length residential sales a month across the nine-county Pennsylvania core, from county deed records. Each is a household that must choose an HVAC, plumbing and electrical provider within months (Punctual Pros ad plan, Oct 6, 2026).
- About 1,150 sales a month on the Jersey Shore (Punctual Pros ad plan).
- About one in three Pennsylvania core buyers bought a pre-1980 home (Punctual Pros ad plan).
- The plan assumes a 1.0% lead rate per mail piece. It sets this below the 4-5% prospect response rate the ANA reports. This is an assumption, not a measured rate (Punctual Pros ad plan).
- Lancaster is one of the nine core counties and holds a confirmed tri-brand site on Running Pump Rd (Punctual Pros market profile, Sep 24, 2026).

## Prospects versus leads

"New movers" and "leads" are different things:

| Measure | PA core (all nine counties) | Lancaster County |
|---|---|---|
| New-mover households per month | ~2,300 | Not in context |
| Mail leads per month at 1.0% | ~23 (est.) | Not in context |

The ~23 is simple arithmetic on the plan's assumed rate. Treat it as an estimate until the mail test reads out.

## Why not prorate

- One shortcut would be to split the 2,300 by Lancaster's share of households. The market profile gives about 965k occupied homes for the core, but the excerpt does not show Lancaster's share.
- Sales volume also may not track households, so a prorated figure could mislead.
- The Census building permits snapshot does not list Lancaster among the counties shown. Permits measure new construction, not resales, so they would not answer this question anyway.

## Data that would answer it

- Lancaster County deed records filtered to arm's-length residential sales, by month. This is the same source the plan used for the core total.
- ServiceTitan tracking-number and QR responses from mail drop 1, read by Lancaster zip. This gives actual leads rather than modelled ones.
- The Lancaster share of the pre-1980 buyer segment, which the plan uses to target the Ben Franklin offer.

## Next actions

- Pull the Lancaster County deed extract for the last 12 months. Report monthly arm's-length residential sales and the pre-1980 share.
- Cut mail drop 1 response by county in ServiceTitan. Report Lancaster leads and booked jobs against the 10% new-mover holdout.
- Replace the 1.0% lead-rate assumption with the measured Lancaster response once the week-4 read is in.
- Add a county column to the new-mover list so later questions like this one can be answered directly.
